obligations.text: Saving an installed module's <Name>.ZPM document updates the stored module record at once.
obligations.cases: existing record; valid save vs refused save
obligations.observation: stored module record after Save returns

obligations.text: A valid edit replaces the record version, and a lower version is accepted on this path.
obligations.cases: valid edit with higher vs lower version
obligations.observation: record version after save; save status

obligations.text: A valid edit replaces the other manifest fields of the record.
obligations.cases: valid edit changing a non-version field (e.g. Description, dependencies) vs unchanged
obligations.observation: record fields other than version after save
obligations.gap: Record models only name, version and resource count, and update() copies every non-version field from the old record (..r). A save that left Description or dependencies at their old values satisfies the model equally. Reader: module record fields after StudioDocument/Module.cls::UpdatePersistentFromStream.

obligations.text: Saving an empty document keeps the record and its resources and sets the version to 0.0.1+snapshot.
obligations.cases: empty vs valid document on an existing record

obligations.text: Deleting the document deletes the module record and leaves the module's code in the namespace.
obligations.cases: delete vs keep
obligations.observation: record presence and namespace classes after Delete

obligations.text: As built (C:D44), a refused save such as malformed XML empties the stored document text while the record keeps the earlier manifest. Graded as the as-built claim.
obligations.cases: malformed vs valid document
obligations.observation: save status, stored document text, record

obligations.text: As built (C:D45), a manifest naming a different module is accepted under the old name: the record takes the other fields and the document keeps the new name. Graded as the as-built claim. The other fields are represented by version only; the general field gap is #3.
obligations.cases: document naming the same vs a different module
obligations.observation: save status, record name and version, stored document name

obligations.text: A <ModuleReference> with no version accepts any version. The exact/range semantics are owned by version.range and the selection by deps (not counted here).
obligations.cases: reference with omitted Version vs an exact version, against offers including a prerelease
obligations.observation: which offered versions the reference accepts
obligations.gap: iteration34 versions.rs treats E::Any as satisfied by every version, but the mapping from an omitted <Version> in Storage/ModuleReference to E::Any is not modeled, and eligible() excludes prerelease offers unless the prerelease flag is set, which the block does not qualify. Contrast: dependency without Version against offers {1.0.0, 2.0.0-beta} must show which is accepted at the resolver.

units.P1: excluded: definition of <SystemRequirements>; the refusal outcome restates load.refusal.requirements (owner not yet enumerated, chunk B)

obligations.text: A Version system requirement refuses an IRIS version the module does not support.
obligations.cases: current IRIS version inside vs outside the declared Version expression
obligations.gap: No formal rule covers Storage/SystemRequirements.cls::CheckVersion (or VersionStringSet). iteration3 requirement_failures omits Version. Contrast: Version=">=2099.1" vs ">=2020.1" on the same instance must give refusal vs success.

obligations.text: IPMVersion and PythonVersion requirements refuse an IPM or Python version outside the declared expression (mapped-namespace reader gap owned by namespace.version.mapped-reader).
obligations.cases: installed IPM/Python version inside vs outside the expression
obligations.gap: No formal rule covers CheckIPMVersion or CheckPythonVersion/GetPythonVersion. Contrast: IPMVersion=">=99.0.0" vs ">=0.9.0" must give refusal vs success.

parent.entailment: Interoperability, Health and SYSNamespace bullets restate rules owned by module.requirement.values and are aliased there. Version, IPMVersion and PythonVersion are parent-only obligations (#1, #2) with no child that entails them, so they stay open. The refusal outcome belongs to load.refusal.requirements. No obligation is credited by composition.

obligations.gap: The spec gives no Health failure for Unset, and neighbors plus control unset-health-means-false exercise only the Health instance. No neighbor or control exercises Unset on a non-Health instance (a rule requiring Health when unset would still verify).

obligations.text: Explicit Health false excludes Health products.
obligations.cases: Health=false on a Health instance vs unset
obligations.basis: reused:.g5/ontology/features/manifest.g5.md metadata module.requirement.values (resources.rs requirement_failures, requirement_neighbors; iter3 controls in run_models.py)

obligations.text: SYSNamespace="true" requires the exact %SYS namespace. False or omission adds no namespace restriction.
obligations.cases: true in USER vs %SYS; unset in USER
obligations.basis: reused:.g5/ontology/features/manifest.g5.md metadata module.requirement.values (resources.rs requirement_failures, requirement_neighbors; iter3 controls in run_models.py)

obligations.text: The aggregate appends returned errors from its checks in order rather than stopping after the first returned error.
obligations.cases: several failing checks vs one
obligations.observation: ordered list of failures in the CheckRequirements status
obligations.basis: reused:.g5/ontology/features/manifest.g5.md metadata module.requirement.values (resources.rs requirement_failures, requirement_neighbors; iter3 controls in run_models.py)
obligations.gap: The three-failure neighbor proves order among Interoperability, Health and SYSNamespace only. CheckRequirements also appends CheckVersion, CheckIPMVersion and CheckPythonVersion (product order Version, Interoperability, Health, IPMVersion, PythonVersion, SYSNamespace), which the model omits. Contrast: Version and SYSNamespace both failing must report both, Version first.

obligations.text: A thrown exception may stop later checks. Version parsing, runtime detection and SemVer exceptions are separate dependencies.
obligations.cases: a check that throws vs returns an error
obligations.gap: No model represents a throwing check. Contrast: CheckVersion throwing on an unparsable expression stops CheckSYSNamespace vs a returned error that does not.

obligations.cases: <Default> vs <Parameter> value, read by an Invoke argument vs by the installer class

obligations.text: A -D<name>=<value> on the command line overrides the declared value.
obligations.cases: declared default/parameter with vs without -D
obligations.observation: value seen by Invoke and installer readers

obligations.text: Dotted parameter names become nested parameters.
obligations.cases: name a.b vs a
obligations.observation: subscript structure seen by the reader
obligations.gap: No formal rule maps a dotted -D or <Default> name to nested parameter subscripts. Contrast: -Da.b=1 read as pParams("a","b") vs a flat "a.b" key by a resource attribute or installer.

obligations.text: Placeholders in parameter values are filled in, repeatedly if needed.
obligations.cases: chain a=${b}, b=${c}, c=v in forward vs backward declaration order
obligations.gap: resolve_bounded iterates passes to a fixed point and inputs.rs parameter_neighbors shows one sweep resolves a forward chain but not a backward one, but no theorem shows resolve_bounded resolves a multi-level backward chain (native E22, E31, E36 only). Reader: Storage/ModuleSetting/Default.cls::ResolvePlaceholders.

parent.entailment: The parent owns delivery, -D precedence, dotted names and repeated filling (#1-#4). The children own expression syntax, literal values and cycles. No parent obligation is entailed by the children, so none is credited by composition.

obligations.text: Parameter names match regardless of case.

obligations.gap: with_builtins proves a supplied builtin map wins, but which names are built in is an input. Storage/Module.cls::%Evaluate sets the five customParams after GetCustomParameters, and the model does not tie that list. Contrast: a default named version vs one named other (native E20).

obligations.text: The same forms give instance values namespace, namespaceLower and mgrDir.
obligations.cases: namespace vs namespaceLower vs mgrDir; local parameter of the same name

obligations.text: #{expression} gives the value of an ObjectScript expression, or nothing if it fails.

The stated order also contradicts the source: Storage/Module.cls::%Evaluate runs %EvaluateMacro before ResolvePlaceholders/EvaluateAttribute, then system expressions, {name} and #{}. Contrast: a parameter whose value contains $$$name gives an unexpanded macro if lookup follows macro expansion.

obligations.text: If parameters refer to each other in a loop, IPM should report an error naming the circular reference instead of installing with an unfilled value. Intended promise; the as-built model refutes it (C:D3).

obligations.text: As built, a=${b}, b=${a} returns unresolved ${a} without the error, while a=${b}, b=ok returns ok.
obligations.cases: cyclic vs resolving neighbor
obligations.gap: cycle_witness proves only that no circular error is raised. Neither the returned value ${a} for the cycle nor ok for the resolving neighbor is asserted (native E30 only). Reader: Storage/ModuleSetting/Default.cls::ResolvePlaceholders result.

obligations.text: Using the unresolved value later may raise a regular-expression error, which does not satisfy the circular-reference requirement.
obligations.cases: later use of ${a} vs resolved value
obligations.observation: error kind at the later reader
obligations.gap: replacement() fails on $ not followed by 0/1, and matched_dollar_can_fail exercises $5, but no theorem connects a cycle's unresolved ${a} to a later regex failure (native E18, E35 only).

obligations.gap: command() takes a Seq<FileInput>; splitting the -env argument at ; (Lifecycle/Base.cls LoadEnvironmentConfig callers) is not modeled. Contrast: "a.json;b.json" loads two files in order.

obligations.cases: VAR set vs unset

obligations.cases: nested path present vs absent vs through a scalar
obligations.gap: lookup is specified, but only the scalar-on-path absence is proved. No theorem shows a loaded nested value returned by GetArg, and no binding ties lookup to GetArg's body.

obligations.text: A missing -env file is an error.
obligations.cases: missing vs readable file

obligations.text: Files merge in order; a later value replaces an earlier one and nested objects merge key by key.
obligations.cases: overlapping vs disjoint keys across two files

obligations.text: Every command that runs module phases starts from an empty configuration and loads only its own -env files; a later command in the same session does not see an earlier command's files.
obligations.cases: load -env f then test without -env in one shell session
obligations.observation: configuration read by the second command
obligations.gap: command() is defined to start empty, but which commands clear and load (Lifecycle/Base.cls Reload phase, Main.cls phase commands) is not modeled. A phase-running path that skips LoadEnvironmentConfig satisfies the model. Contrast: native S1 (second command reads empty).

obligations.text: While a configuration is loaded, IPM compiles in one process so code generated at compile time can read it.
obligations.cases: configuration loaded vs empty

obligations.text: An environment value is inserted literally. As built, a $ or \ in the value changes or breaks the result (C:D14).
obligations.cases: value a$1b, a\b, a$9b vs plain
obligations.gap: dollar_is_not_literal proves the ICU replacement semantics, but evaluate_json takes the substitution as an input, so no rule connects an environment value to that replacement text. Contrast: ${CONS_VAR}=a$9b makes the load fail while =ab succeeds (native U7, U8).

obligations.text: Object elements in arrays merge recursively at the same index; primitive arrays merge by position, so a later array cannot remove items.
A missing or malformed later file clears earlier values and raises; each LoadEnvironmentConfig call clears first, so the failed command keeps nothing from any file.
obligations.cases: good file then bad file vs two good files; array root

obligations.text: Process-local configuration reaches a same-process compile, while a fresh worker process starts empty.
obligations.cases: same process vs fresh worker
